note: Faithful rendering of the general/specific and figurative/literal characteristics of the four truths and the two kinds of those seeking liberation; 'direct/indirect' for drang po / drang po ma yin is a defensible choice.

errors.english: because that which causes destruction does not abide, owing to its own abidance
errors.why: The reason given is that when the destroyer is not present the thing abides by itself, so a cause of its abiding is pointless; the English makes the destroyer the one that does not abide.

errors.english: The summary is intended to be expressed as non-exhaustive
errors.why: lhag dang bcas pa means the summary is meant to include a surplus (what is implied as well as what is stated), as the following gloss says, not that it is non-exhaustive.

errors.english: the connecting mental consciousness
errors.why: mtshams sbyor ba is the technical term for rebirth-linking (pratisandhi); 'connecting' loses the doctrinal point that the rebirth-linking mental consciousness is the sattva.

note: The commentarial argument is followed in outline but several sentences of the refutation of a substratum and some technical terms are garbled or loosely rendered.

errors.english: wherein these phenomena are neither afflicted nor unafflicted
errors.why: The sutra says these dharmas are without afflictions, they are not afflicted; it does not deny that they are unafflicted.

fix.find: wherein these phenomena are neither afflicted nor unafflicted
fix.replace: wherein these phenomena are without afflictions; they are not afflicted

errors.english: or from which arising does not occur
errors.why: In this list (Buddha-qualities, awakening, path, liberation) 'byung ba is deliverance (niḥsaraṇa), as also in the following ཆོས་ཐམས་ཅད་འབྱུང་བ་ཤེས་ནས, rendered 'source of all phenomena'.

note: Good rendering of the commentary and the Akṣayamati citation, apart from a reversed clause on the afflictions and a misread 'byung ba.

errors.english: The clay materials used for washing should be kept in a pottery shard.
errors.why: lci ba is cow dung, the material for the plastering substance ('dag rdzas), to be kept on a potsherd; it is neither clay nor for washing.

fix.find: The clay materials used for washing should be kept in a pottery shard.
fix.replace: The cow dung used as plastering material should be kept on a potsherd.

errors.english: Udayin had them establish temporary lodgings for him
errors.why: gnas 'char ba is the Vinaya term for requesting/taking dependence (niśraya); Udāyin had the new monks take dependence on him, which is why they are then called his attendants (nye gnas).

fix.find: Udayin had them establish temporary lodgings for him
fix.replace: Udayin had them take dependence (niśraya) on him

errors.english: Except for those [note: grasses] that are clean and not sprouting
errors.why: Continuing srog chags from the previous side, the exception is for grass in which living creatures have not bred; 'clean' and 'sprouting' are not in the text.

note: The narrative of the expulsion rule is well told, but the Vinaya technical vocabulary (dung plaster, taking dependence) is misread in places.

errors.english: (Upali) the Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of monastic law replied, "They should be given."
errors.why: Upāli is the one who asked; nye ba 'khor is the vocative in the Buddha's answer: 'Upāli, it should be given.'

fix.find: (Upali) the Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of monastic law replied, "They should be given."
fix.replace: The Buddha replied, "Upāli, they should be given."

errors.english: the son will not return as the master of the father's house
errors.why: The reason is that the expelled son does not cease to be an owner of the father's household, which is why one may accept from him.

fix.find: the son will not return as the master of the father's house
fix.replace: the son does not cease to be an owner of the father's house

errors.english: From the inquiry of the daughter of a Brahmin monk
errors.why: The questioner is the brahmin's daughter (a nun), not the daughter of a monk.

note: A difficult Vinaya commentary rendered with partial success; the question-and-answer roles and the reasoning about the expelled son are inverted.
Accurate and careful rendering of the analysis of past, future and present mind and the plantain-tree example.

errors.english: he is driven by the flow of passion and called 'master'
errors.why: Candra is asserting that, in every respect, it is their father the king who is lord of the provinces; nothing depicts the father as driven by passion.

note: A readable rendering of difficult kāvya; the obscure gnomic verses are handled plausibly, with one doubtful sentence in Candra's speech.

errors.english: Experiencing the taste of the pain of perfect peace
errors.why: bde ba is bliss: he tasted the bliss of perfect peace.

fix.find: the taste of the pain of perfect peace
fix.replace: the taste of the bliss of perfect peace

errors.english: The one who had relied on the householder [note: referring to the king's previous companion or the ascetic himself in a different role] became unhappy
errors.why: The subject is the Bodhisattva who has just left the country, disheartened with lay life and its dependence; the English invents a different person with a speculative note.

errors.english: How could a single person perform so many infinite, individual actions at one time?
errors.why: The verse rebuts a single creator: how could one being make countless separate things (dngos po) at once.

note: The wrong views of the ministers are set out clearly; one striking reversal (pain for bliss) and a confused opening sentence.

errors.english: What is called "impossibility otherwise" the necessity that the effect cannot exist without the cause
errors.why: The gloss restricting anyathānupapatti to effect and cause is unmarked and wrong; the inseparability is not limited to causal reasons.

fix.find: What is called "impossibility otherwise" the necessity that the effect cannot exist without the cause

errors.english: The engagement does not occur because of certainty.
errors.why: The phyir is final: even though the three modes are present, the reason does not function to produce certainty.

fix.find: The engagement does not occur because of certainty.
fix.replace: It does not operate so as to yield certainty.

errors.english: never exist separately
errors.why: The verse says the reason's force never lies in the three modes (because it lies in inseparability), not that the modes never exist separately.

errors.english: This is the second characteristic.
errors.why: In context of reasons with one or more characteristics, this marks the moon example as a reason having two characteristics, not 'the second characteristic'.

errors.english: One knows with certainty: "This was created."
errors.why: One knows with certainty that this sensation was produced by the mosquito; the English splits the clause and loses the agent.

errors.english: Even if the property of the subject (paksadharmatā) is a non-entity
errors.why: The point is that the reason proves even when the property of the subject is actually absent, not that it is a non-entity.

note: The verses on anyathānupapatti versus the three modes are followed overall, but several logical clauses are misconstrued and an unmarked gloss narrows the key term.

errors.english: If one is free of that heart-tormenting anger
errors.why: The stanza (contrasted with the next, on fame waxing like the moon) says that one in the grip of anger is shunned and gets ill repute; the English makes freedom from anger the condition for ill repute.

note: A fluent, largely faithful verse rendering of the Bodhisattva's discourse on anger, with one incoherent stanza.
